infos.prompt: Nesh-Deeka wants the jar you carried off the camp.
lines: No. That jar holds sap of Nine Bends, my own tree. It is not for Nesh-Deeka to take. If you lick the sap, the Hist shows you a vision.
I mean to lick it and hear my tree once, before anyone takes it from me. The jar is locked in my lockbox among the crates under the lanterns. I keep the key on me. So what are you to me?
A reason, a price or a fight?

infos.prompt: What did you see at the cutting?
lines: I saw them come ashore at night. They were the cutters, the people who cut a Hist's roots. Each carried empty jars.
They went straight to the roots of the camp's cutting, the slip of the Hist that grew there. They cut the roots and filled the jars from the cuts. They were quick and quiet.
One jar rolled away by the fire. I took it before I thought. I knew it was Nine Bends the moment I held it.

infos.prompt: (Persuade) The one I work for means to find who cut your tree. We can learn it from the jar.
lines: You speak as if you mean it. I wanted one taste of my tree before the jar was taken from me. I wanted it badly. But I want more to know who cut Nine Bends. Find who did it. That is all I ask of you.
Here is the key. The jar is in my lockbox, among the crates under the lanterns. I go back to my months with empty hands. Do not make me sorry.

infos.prompt: (Persuade) The one I work for means to find who cut your tree. We can learn it from the jar.

infos.prompt: What will you do without the jar?
lines: I will work off my months as before. I have a shift, my food and my sleep, and that will not change. I meant to taste Nine Bends once.

infos.prompt: What does the Reed want of me?
lines: I want the cutters' jar, the one Dives-Without-A-Rope carried off the camp. I mean to learn from it what the cutters wanted.
It is in the hold of the ship of Buys-The-Months, at the pier at Hereguard Plantation, west of Lilmoth. Go west along the shore, a fair way, past the old lighthouse.
Dives-Without-A-Rope keeps it in the hold. How you get it is your affair. Look over the hold before you decide. Then bring the jar to me here.

infos.prompt: Here is the jar Dives-Without-A-Rope carried off the camp.
lines: That is the jar. Let me draw the stopper. The sap is fresh from the roots. It was drawn into a jar that the cutters brought with them, so they mean to keep it. This is a long work, not a raid.
Whoever tastes Hist sap sees a vision. A stranger may see something else. I do not know which you are. I will write while you put one drop on your tongue. Will you taste it?

infos.prompt: (Alchemy) Let me read the sap first, as a tester does, then taste it.
lines: You read it as a tester does. Good. It is fresh sap, drawn from cut roots. The stopper and the neck of the jar show the marks of other jars filled beside it. I will note that.
Then you tasted, and I wrote what you said while you were under it. A ship's hold with roots through its deck. A door that was never built, and a voice, dry, that made no words.
I cannot tell you what it means, and I will not guess. Keep the page and twenty-five gold, and I will keep the jar. We pay our hands.
One more thing, because you are one of mine now: the Hist at Low-Reed, a village east of here, has turned its face from its people.
